docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
The best known of Sanskrit plays: King Duṣyanta meets Śakuntalā at the hermitage of Kaṇva, marries her, forgets her under a curse and recognises her by a ring. The king and the learned characters speak Sanskrit; the women and most other characters speak Prakrit, as the conventions of the stage required. The English translation by Arthur W. Ryder is on the shelf Classics in Translation.

From Wikisource · Public domain

Kālidāsa, Abhijñānaśākuntalam: the Sanskrit and Prakrit text as transcribed on Sanskrit Wikisource by its contributors.
